    Length functions on abelian categories #

    The manuscript works in mod Λ, where every object has finite length, and uses this through finiteness arguments: traces are finite sums of images, rejects finite intersections of kernels (Lemma 2.9), and every module is a finite direct sum of indecomposables. We package what is needed as a length function: a natural number attached to each object which vanishes exactly on zero objects and decreases strictly along non-invertible monomorphisms and epimorphisms. Both target categories, finite-dimensional modules over a finite-dimensional algebra and representations of the linear quiver, carry one.

    From this we derive that every nonempty set of subobjects of an object has maximal and minimal elements, which replaces Lemma 2.9.

    class PretorsionImageClosed.HasLength (C : Type u_1) [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms C] :
    Type u_1

    A length function on a category with zero morphisms: length X = 0 exactly for zero objects, and length decreases strictly along monomorphisms and epimorphisms that are not isomorphisms.

    • length : C → ℕ

      The length of an object.

    • length_eq_zero_iff (X : C) : length X = 0 ↔ CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero X
    • length_eq_of_iso {X Y : C} : ∀ (a : X ≅ Y), length X = length Y
    • length_lt_of_mono {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : CategoryTheory.Mono f → ¬CategoryTheory.IsIso f → length X < length Y
    • length_lt_of_epi {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : CategoryTheory.Epi f → ¬CategoryTheory.IsIso f → length Y < length X
